question: Should experimental Claw updates be allowed to mutate shared package/plugin installations, MCP config, Gateway cron jobs, workspace files, and root provenance under the proposed consent-bound partial-recovery contract?
rationale: Tests can validate mechanics, but they cannot decide whether OpenClaw should adopt this broad shared-resource ownership model or accept externally mutated artifacts that cannot always be rolled back.

options.title: Approve after complete live proof
options.body: Accept the gated contract once current-head package, cron, consent-digest, partial-state, and recovery evidence is posted and reviewed with the full stack.

options.title: Narrow the mutation boundary
options.body: Limit the first update release to reversible agent and workspace changes while deferring shared package, MCP, and cron mutation.

options.title: Pause the apply slice
options.body: Keep update planning read-only until the RFC establishes a different ownership and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Approve after complete live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the gated contract once current-head package, cron, consent-digest, partial-state, and recovery evidence is posted and reviewed with the full stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the proposed RFC implementation stack and is the strongest available routing candidate, although final product approval must come from an OpenClaw maintainer.
